chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Fajr. When he finished, he turned his face toward his companions and asked whether a group of people had attended. They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: Are they away (travelling)? They said: No. He said: Know that there is no prayer harder on the hypocrites than this prayer (Fajr) and Isha.

key_terms.العشاء: Isha — the night prayer, the last of the five daily prayers
key_terms.الفجر: Fajr — the pre-dawn obligatory prayer, one of the five daily prayers, performed before sunrise
key_terms.المنافقين: al-Munafiqun — the hypocrites; in Islamic usage, those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly disbelieve or lack commitment
key_terms.انصرف: He finished (the prayer) — technical term indicating completion of salat and the formal turning away

ai.seo_question: Which prayers are hardest on hypocrites according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a prophetic hadith in which the Prophet (SAWW), after completing the Fajr prayer, noticed the absence of certain individuals among his companions. Upon learning they were not travelling, he declared that Fajr and Isha prayers are the most burdensome prayers for hypocrites. This teaching reveals that hypocrites avoid the two prayers at the extremities of the day — when it is most inconvenient — since they lack sincere faith to motivate them. The Companions of the Prophet would have understood this as a warning against the condition of hypocrisy, which manifests in abandoning congregational prayer particularly at difficult times.
